ELI5: Why are people susceptible to motion sickness?

Motion Sickness is thought to arise when there is a mismatch between the signals being sent by your eyes and your inner ear to your brain.

Usually your brain incorporates information being sent from both sources to know where you are and how you are moving. If this process gets interrupted, then your brain becomes confused, leading to the symptoms experienced by suffers of motion sickness.

The easiest way to understand this confusion is by thinking about what your eyes and inner ear are telling your brain, when you are travelling in a car.

Your eyes are telling your brain that you are moving really fast, but your inner ear, which is responsible for balance, is telling your brain you are not moving at all, that you are sitting perfectly still.

I think you have the last bit somewhat off. Your inner ear can tell you're moving in a car, but has issues matching the speed with what it's seeing... this is especially true when you're looking at something stationary like reading or playing a game.

Also, this reaction is thought to have evolved as a reaction to poisons. When poisoned you'll often have symptoms like tunnel vision and dizziness.

Your inner ear is responsible for detecting your position and orientation in 3 dimensional space. It is how you tell up from down.

When you are in a car, your body is sitting still in the seat, in an upright position. Your eyes are telling your brain that you are moving. Your inner ear is telling your brain that you aren't moving; it is not having to make any of the fine adjustments to your balance that it would normally have to do, if you were walking or running. As far as it is concerned, your body is stationary.

Hence the confusion.

Motion sickness basically results from a mismatch of sensory input.

For instance, when you're in a car with the windows down, reading a book, and driving in a situation that requires continual speed changes, your body can feel that it is accelerating, but your eyes do not see movement.

Historically, these mismatches were usually caused by poisons. So, when your body senses a sufficient mismatch, it gets worried and starts trying to purge the poisons.

Would motion sickness ever occur in humans before technological inventions such as boats (or other machinery)?

Either, 1) motion sickness is an adaptation that "told us: 'motion is bad" (e.g. swaying heavily in a tree during a storm [or hammock attached to trees, etc.])

Or, 2) it would be found in other animals under like circumstance; in which case it is likely just a 'fuck-up' where nature never encountered the problem in the first place: the technology to induce motion sickness is so new it never really applied to natural selection (it never effected survivability on a day-to-day basis and/or killed enough of the population to matter), so it was never selected for--if motion sickness caused death it would be a different story.

The fact that we all get motion sickness (animals too) suggests that it was simply not a factor in any relevant natural selection -- and not severe enough at present to cause any actual notable change. Motion sickness was/is never selected for/against; it never happened until 'now', and since our evolutionary basis came before its advent -- and since it does not effect survival or breeding -- that 'evolutionary basis' [our pre-ship-building makeup] never had to change in concern to it.... A discomfort we have to deal with because [insert inner ear/brain scientist comment--aka "pre-ship-building makeup].

Very simply put, motion sickness occurs when there is conflicting information sent to your brain by different sensory organs. Due to the conflicting information, the brain deduces that you are hallucinating and furthermore assumes that you hallucinate because you are afflicted by a neurotoxin. As this toxin may have been induced into the body by eating something poisonous, the brain then produces nausea in you in an attempt to have you vomit out whatever stomach content might cause the poisoning.

How exactly motion sickness works depends on the source - if you're playing a video game, your eyes and ears may register movement and sounds that indicate movement but the other sensory organs register you as standing still. In a car, the so-called vestibular system (a structure in your inner ear that is responsible for monitoring the bodies balance and position) registers movement but other sensory organs don't. This is also the reason why reading a book while riding a car might worsen the motion sickness - the more conflicting signals the brain gets, the more it will try to flush out what it assumes to be poison.
